# Case 1: empty graph (0 nodes)
{"nodes":0,"edges":{},"totalWeight":0}
@ 0 nodes → empty partition
{"partition":[]}

# Case 2: single-node graph
{"nodes":1,"edges":{"0":[]},"totalWeight":0}
@ 1 node → [0]
{"partition":[0]}

# Case 3: three-node graph with some edges
{"nodes":3,"edges":{"0":[{"to":1,"weight":1.0}],"1":[{"to":0,"weight":1.0},{"to":2,"weight":0.5}],"2":[{"to":1,"weight":0.5}]},"totalWeight":1.5}
@ InitSingletonPartition should ignore edges and just return [0,1,2]
{"partition":[0,1,2]}

# Case 4: five-node graph, arbitrary edges
{"nodes":5,"edges":{"0":[{"to":1,"weight":1.0}],"1":[{"to":0,"weight":1.0},{"to":2,"weight":1.0},{"to":3,"weight":0.5}],"2":[{"to":1,"weight":1.0},{"to":4,"weight":0.2}],"3":[{"to":1,"weight":0.5}],"4":[{"to":2,"weight":0.2}]},"totalWeight":3.7}
@ regardless of topology, each node gets its own cluster → [0,1,2,3,4]
{"partition":[0,1,2,3,4]}
